# 93 Hepatic Tumors in Childhood

1. **Which is the most common primary hepatic tumor of childhood?**  
    A. Hepatocellular carcinoma  
    B. Mesenchymal hamartoma  
    C. Rhabdomyosarcoma  
    **D. Hepatoblastoma**  
    *Correct: D. Hepatoblastomas are the most common primary hepatic tumors of childhood, constituting 43% to 64% of all hepatic neoplasms.*

2. **What percentage of primary hepatic tumors in children younger than 5 years is accounted for by hepatoblastoma?**  
    A. 50-60%  
    **B. 91-96%**  
    C. 75-80%  
    D. 30-40%  
    *Correct: B. Hepatoblastoma accounts for 91% to 96% of primary hepatic tumors in children younger than 5 years.*

3. **Which of the following is the most common benign hepatic tumor in childhood?**  
    A. Focal nodular hyperplasia  
    B. Hepatocellular adenoma  
    C. Mesenchymal hamartoma  
    **D. Hemangioma**  
    *Correct: D. Vascular tumors (hemangiomas) account for 56.8% of benign hepatic tumors in childhood.*

4. **What percentage of benign hepatic tumors in childhood is represented by mesenchymal hamartoma?**  
    A. 56.8%  
    **B. 28.9%**  
    C. 7.5%  
    D. 6.7%  
    *Correct: B. Mesenchymal hamartoma accounts for 28.9% of benign hepatic tumors in childhood.*

5. **Hepatocellular carcinoma accounts for what percentage of pediatric liver tumors?**  
    A. Less than 5%  
    B. 10-15%  
    **C. 22-23%**  
    D. 35-40%  
    *Correct: C. Hepatocellular carcinoma accounts for 22% to 23% of pediatric liver tumors.*

6. **Which of the following is true about hepatocellular carcinoma in children?**  
    A. It is the most common liver tumor in infants  
    B. It accounts for over 50% of liver tumors in children under 5 years  
    **C. It is rare in infancy**  
    D. It comprises over 10% of hepatic malignancies in adult age groups  
    *Correct: C. Hepatocellular carcinoma is rare in infancy.*

7. **What is the approximate incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in children in the United States?**  
    A. 0.1 cases per 1 million children  
    **B. 1.2 cases per 1 million children**  
    C. 5.0 cases per 1 million children  
    D. 10.5 cases per 1 million children  
    *Correct: B. Approximately 1.2 cases per 1 million children exist in the United States.*

8. **Which of the following tumor types constitutes 14% of malignant liver tumors occurring in children 6 to 10 years of age?**  
    A. Hepatocellular carcinoma  
    B. Rhabdomyosarcoma  
    **C. Embryonal sarcoma**  
    D. Fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma  
    *Correct: C. Embryonal sarcoma constitutes 14% of malignant liver tumors occurring in children 6 to 10 years of age.*

9. **What is the typical age range for diagnosis of embryonal sarcoma?**  
    A. Infancy  
    B. 1-5 years  
    **C. 5-16 years**  
    D. Adolescence and adulthood  
    *Correct: C. The age at diagnosis for embryonal sarcoma ranges from 5 to 16 years.*

10. **Which staging system is used for primary malignant liver tumors of childhood?**  
    A. TNM staging  
    **B. PRETEXT staging**  
    C. Child-Pugh staging  
    D. BCLC staging  
    *Correct: B. PRETEXT (PRE-Treatment EXTent) is the staging system used for primary malignant liver tumors of childhood.*

11. **Which of the following is NOT a component of the diagnostic evaluation for suspected liver tumors in children?**  
    A. Complete blood count  
    B. Liver function tests  
    C. Coagulation studies  
    **D. Bone scan**  
    *Correct: D. The diagnostic evaluation should include a complete blood count, liver function tests, coagulation studies, and tumor markers (serum AFP and β-hCG), but bone scan is not specifically mentioned as a standard component.*

12. **Which tumor marker is essential in the evaluation of pediatric liver tumors?**  
    A. CA-19-9  
    B. CEA  
    **C. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)**  
    D. Carcinoembryonic antigen  
    *Correct: C. Serum AFP is an essential tumor marker in the evaluation of pediatric liver tumors.*

13. **What imaging modality provides the greatest amount of information concerning liver lesions and surrounding veins and bile ducts?**  
    A. Ultrasound  
    B. CT scan  
    **C. MRI**  
    D. PET scan  
    *Correct: C. At present, MRI provides the greatest amount of information concerning the lesion and surrounding veins and bile ducts.*

14. **Which of the following is true regarding fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (FLH)?**  
    A. It is more common in infants  
    B. It has a worse prognosis than standard HCC  
    **C. It tends to grow as a single mass compared to the early multifocality of standard HCC**  
    D. It accounts for the majority of HCC cases in children  
    *Correct: C. The tendency of FLH to grow slowly, as a single mass, compared with the early multifocality of standard HCC.*

15. **What percentage of patients with fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma may present with tumor rupture and hemoperitoneum?**  
    A. 1%  
    B. 5%  
    **C. 10%**  
    D. 25%  
    *Correct: C. Despite its typically slow growth, 10% of patients with FLH may present with tumor rupture and hemoperitoneum.*

16. **Which of the following liver tumors is most commonly associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome?**  
    **A. Hepatoblastoma**  
    B. Hepatocellular carcinoma  
    C. Mesenchymal hamartoma  
    D. Hemangioma  
    *Correct: A. Hepatoblastoma is associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome.*

17. **Which of the following is a risk factor for hepatocellular adenoma in children?**  
    A. Hepatitis B infection  
    B. Cirrhosis  
    **C. Type I glycogen storage disease**  
    D. Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency  
    *Correct: C. Hepatic adenomas are expected with type I glycogen storage disease after the first decade of life and may be multiple.*

18. **What is the recommended management for hepatic adenomas in children?**  
    A. Observation only  
    B. Chemotherapy  
    **C. Resection**  
    D. Radiation therapy  
    *Correct: C. It is best to remove adenomas because of the difficulty of differentiating them from low-grade HCCs, uncertainty about future malignant degeneration, and the possibility of rupture and hemorrhage.*

19. **Which of the following is the most common site for colon cancer metastasis in children?**  
    A. Liver  
    **B. Peritoneal surfaces**  
    C. Lungs  
    D. Bones  
    *Correct: B. The pattern of spread for colon cancer in children is over peritoneal surfaces, rather than through the portal system, and hepatic metastases usually occur late despite massive peritoneal disease.*

20. **Which of the following is true about rhabdoid tumors of the liver?**  
    A. They are the most common liver tumors in children  
    B. They have an excellent prognosis with standard chemotherapy  
    **C. They are rare, aggressive, and poorly responsive to standard cytotoxic chemotherapy**  
    D. They are always primary to the liver  
    *Correct: C. Rhabdoid tumors of the liver are rare, aggressive, and poorly responsive to standard cytotoxic chemotherapy.*

21. **What is the relative frequency of liver metastases in rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
    A. Most common site  
    B. Second most common site  
    C. Third most common site  
    **D. Follows regional lung, lymph nodes, and bone as a site of metastasis**  
    *Correct: D. The liver follows regional lung, lymph nodes, and bone as a site of rhabdomyosarcoma metastases.*

22. **Which of the following is true about malignant germ cell tumors of the liver?**  
    A. They are the most common primary liver tumors in children  
    B. They are highly resistant to chemotherapy  
    **C. They may respond well to neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by resection**  
    D. They typically require liver transplantation as first-line treatment  
    *Correct: C. In childhood, these may respond well to neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by resection.*

23. **Which chemotherapy regimen is typically used for malignant germ cell tumors of the liver in children?**  
    A. ABVD  
    B. CHOP  
    **C. Cisplatin, ifosfamide, and bleomycin**  
    D. Vincristine, actinomycin D, and cyclophosphamide  
    *Correct: C. Usually, a regimen containing cisplatin, ifosfamide, and bleomycin is used.*

24. **Which of the following is a characteristic feature of mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver?**  
    A. It is most commonly diagnosed in adults  
    **B. Two-thirds are diagnosed in infants younger than 1 year**  
    C. It is typically associated with markedly elevated AFP levels  
    D. It is highly malignant and requires aggressive chemotherapy  
    *Correct: B. Two-thirds of these tumors are diagnosed in infants younger than 1 year, although presentation in the teenage years has been described.*

25. **What is the mean age at diagnosis for mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver?**  
    A. 6 months  
    **B. 16 months**  
    C. 3 years  
    D. 7 years  
    *Correct: B. In one study of 18 such tumors, the mean age at diagnosis was 16 months.*

26. **Which of the following is true about focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) in children?**  
    A. It is the most common benign liver tumor in children  
    B. It is typically associated with oral contraceptive use in children  
    **C. It has been described in children treated for other solid malignancies**  
    D. It frequently undergoes malignant transformation  
    *Correct: C. There has been some attention toward FNH developing in children treated for other solid malignancies. These authors postulated that a vascular injury secondary to chemotherapy or radiation was the causal factor.*

27. **How is focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) distinguished from hepatic adenoma histologically?**  
    **A. Presence of fibrous septa that contain bile ducts and an inflammatory infiltrate**  
    B. Absence of hepatocytes  
    C. Presence of malignant cells  
    D. Absence of Kupffer cells  
    *Correct: A. FNH is distinguished from adenoma by the presence of fibrous septa that contain bile ducts and an inflammatory infiltrate.*

28. **What percentage of unresected hepatic adenomas may develop hepatocellular carcinoma?**  
    A. 1-2%  
    B. 5-10%  
    **C. Approximately 13% (5 of 39)**  
    D. 25-30%  
    *Correct: C. In one report, 5 of 39 unresected hepatic adenomas developed HCC.*

29. **Which of the following is a treatment option for unresectable hepatic adenomas?**  
    A. External beam radiation  
    **B. Embolization**  
    C. Interferon therapy  
    D. Targeted molecular therapy  
    *Correct: B. Embolization of unresectable lesions is mentioned as a treatment option.*

30. **Which of the following is true about hemangioblastoma of the liver?**  
    A. It is the most common benign liver tumor in children  
    **B. It is usually associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease**  
    C. It frequently metastasizes to distant sites  
    D. It is typically treated with chemotherapy  
    *Correct: B. Hemangioblastoma of the liver usually is associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease.*

31. **Which of the following is true about undifferentiated ("embryonal") sarcoma of the liver?**  
    A. It is the most common liver tumor in infants  
    **B. Fewer than 200 cases have been reported in the literature**  
    C. It typically occurs in children younger than 2 years  
    D. It has an excellent prognosis with surgery alone  
    *Correct: B. Fewer than 200 cases of embryonal sarcoma have been reported in the literature.*

32. **What is the most common presentation of biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
    A. Jaundice  
    B. Abdominal pain  
    C. Palpable abdominal mass  
    **D. Intermittent jaundice**  
    *Correct: D. The typical presentation of biliary rhabdomyosarcoma includes intermittent jaundice.*

33. **At what average age is biliary rhabdomyosarcoma typically diagnosed?**  
    A. 6 months  
    B. 1 year  
    **C. 3 years**  
    D. 7 years  
    *Correct: C. Biliary rhabdomyosarcoma is usually diagnosed from 1 to 9 years of age, with an average age of 3 years.*

34. **Which gender is more frequently affected by biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
    **A. Males**  
    B. Females  
    C. Equal incidence in both genders  
    D. Gender predilection is unknown  
    *Correct: A. Biliary rhabdomyosarcoma is seen more frequently in males.*

35. **What is the long-term survival rate for biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
    A. 10-20%  
    B. 30-40%  
    **C. 60-70%**  
    D. 80-90%  
    *Correct: C. Long-term survival is considered to be 60% to 70% and is not dependent on resectability.*

36. **Which of the following is true about angiosarcoma of the liver in children?**  
    A. It is the most common primary liver tumor in children  
    B. It has an excellent response to chemotherapy  
    **C. Evidence of malignant transformation from, or concomitant development with, infantile hemangioma or hemangioendothelioma is found in most cases**  
    D. It is typically diagnosed in infants younger than 6 months  
    *Correct: C. A multi-institutional case series found evidence of either malignant transformation from, or concomitant development with, infantile hemangioma or hemangioendothelioma in 7 of 8 patients.*

37. **What is the outcome for pediatric patients with hepatic angiosarcoma who undergo orthotopic liver transplantation as part of multimodal therapy?**  
    A. Poor, with no long-term survivors reported  
    **B. Better than those not receiving transplantation, with some disease-free survivors**  
    C. Identical to patients receiving chemotherapy alone  
    D. Worse than patients receiving resection alone  
    *Correct: B. Two out of eight patients who underwent orthotopic liver transplantation were the only two patients alive at the time of publication, disease-free at 3.5 years and 5.5 years, respectively.*

38. **Which of the following is the most common malignant liver tumor in children under 5 years of age?**  
    **A. Hepatoblastoma**  
    B. Hepatocellular carcinoma  
    C. Rhabdomyosarcoma  
    D. Embryonal sarcoma  
    *Correct: A. Hepatoblastoma accounts for 91% to 96% of primary hepatic tumors in children younger than 5 years.*

39. **What is the approximate percentage of all hepatic neoplasms in children that hepatoblastoma constitutes?**  
    A. 25-35%  
    **B. 43-64%**  
    C. 65-75%  
    D. 80-90%  
    *Correct: B. Hepatoblastomas are the most common primary hepatic tumors of childhood, constituting 43% to 64% of all hepatic neoplasms in one large series.*

40. **Which of the following is true about the epidemiology of hepatocellular carcinoma in children?**  
    A. It is the most common liver tumor in infants  
    B. It accounts for over 50% of liver tumors in children under 5 years  
    **C. The Liver Cancer Study Group of Japan reported no cases in children age 4 years or younger**  
    D. It comprises over 10% of hepatic malignancies in adult age groups  
    *Correct: C. The Lung Cancer Study Group of Japan reported no cases in children age 4 years or younger in a series of 2286 patients with histologically reviewed tumors.*

41. **Which of the following is a criterion for liver transplantation in children with hepatocellular carcinoma based on extrapolation of Milan criteria?**  
    A. Single tumor no larger than 2 cm in diameter  
    **B. Single tumor no larger than 5 cm in diameter**  
    C. Multiple tumors with the largest measuring less than 3 cm  
    D. Presence of microscopic portal vein invasion is acceptable  
    *Correct: B. The Milan criteria for children stipulate a single tumor no larger than 5 cm in diameter or as many as three tumors each 3 cm or less in diameter.*

42. **Which of the following is NOT part of the Milan criteria for liver transplantation in children with hepatocellular carcinoma?**  
    A. Single tumor no larger than 5 cm in diameter  
    B. Up to three tumors each 3 cm or less in diameter  
    **C. Presence of microscopic portal vein invasion is acceptable**  
    D. Absence of extrahepatic disease  
    *Correct: C. The Milan criteria stipulate an absence of macroscopic portal vein invasions, and absence of extrahepatic disease.*

43. **Which of the following is true about the prognosis of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma compared to standard HCC?**  
    A. It has a worse prognosis than standard HCC  
    **B. When stage is controlled for, the survival is similar between standard HCC and its fibrolamellar variant**  
    C. It has a much better prognosis regardless of stage  
    D. It is always fatal despite treatment  
    *Correct: B. Studies indicate that when stage is controlled for, the survival is similar between standard HCC and its fibrolamellar variant.*

44. **Which of the following liver tumors is associated with type I glycogen storage disease?**  
    A. Hepatoblastoma  
    **B. Hepatocellular adenoma**  
    C. Mesenchymal hamartoma  
    D. Hemangioma  
    *Correct: B. Hepatic adenomas are expected with type I glycogen storage disease after the first decade of life and may be multiple.*

45. **Which of the following is a potential complication of large hepatic hemangiomas in children?**  
    A. Hypoglycemia  
    **B. Congestive heart failure**  
    C. Portal hypertension  
    D. Hepatic encephalopathy  
    *Correct: B. Venous malformations, cavernous hemangiomata, and arteriovenous malformations may be associated with significant shunting that results in congestive heart failure.*

46. **What is the gender distribution of hepatic hemangiomas in children?**  
    A. Equal incidence in both genders  
    **B. More common in girls by 2:1**  
    C. More common in boys by 2:1  
    D. Predominantly affects males  
    *Correct: B. Hepatic hemangiomata are more common in girls by 2:1.*

47. **Which of the following is true about the incidence of vascular lesions as symptomatic hepatic tumors in childhood?**  
    A. They represent 5-10% of symptomatic hepatic tumors  
    **B. They represent 13-18% of symptomatic hepatic tumors**  
    C. They represent 25-30% of symptomatic hepatic tumors  
    D. They represent over 50% of symptomatic hepatic tumors  
    *Correct: B. Vascular lesions taken together represent 13% to 18% of symptomatic hepatic tumors in childhood.*

48. **Which imaging modality is recommended to determine the patency of portal and hepatic veins in the evaluation of liver tumors?**  
    A. Standard X-ray  
    B. CT scan without contrast  
    **C. Doppler US**  
    D. Bone scan  
    *Correct: C. Doppler US is done to determine whether a mass is cystic or solid, determine the patency of the portal and hepatic veins and vena cava, and identify satellite lesions.*

49. **Which of the following is true about the role of thoracic CT in the evaluation of suspected malignant liver tumors in children?**  
    A. It is primarily used to evaluate liver anatomy  
    B. It is used to assess for portal vein thrombosis  
    **C. It is done to evaluate for pulmonary metastases**  
    D. It is used to measure tumor markers  
    *Correct: C. If a malignant tumor is suspected, thoracic CT is done to evaluate for pulmonary metastases.*

50. **Which of the following is the most common cause of death in children with unresectable malignant liver tumors?**  
    A. Renal failure  
    B. Cardiac complications  
    **C. Local tumor effects including biliary sepsis**  
    D. Hemorrhage  
    *Correct: C. Malignant tumors of the extrahepatic biliary tract often cause death due to the effects of local invasion, including biliary sepsis.*

51. **Which of the following is true about the PRETEXT staging system for pediatric liver tumors?**  
    A. It is identical to the TNM staging system used for adults  
    **B. It was developed by the SIOPEL group**  
    C. It is primarily used for benign liver tumors  
    D. It is based solely on tumor size  
    *Correct: B. PRETEXT (PRE-Treatment EXTent) is a staging system for primary malignant liver tumours of childhood developed by the SIOPEL group.*

52. **How many sections does the liver get divided into for PRETEXT staging?**  
    A. 2  
    B. 3  
    **C. 4  
    D. 6**  
    *Correct: C. The PRETEXT staging criteria refer to "sections" of the liver, and the criteria involve up to four sections.*

53. **In PRETEXT staging, what does Stage I indicate?**  
    **A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free**  
    B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free  
    C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free  
    D. All four sections are involved  
    *Correct: A. PRETEXT Stage I: One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free.*

54. **In PRETEXT staging, what does Stage IV indicate?**  
    A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free  
    B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free  
    C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free  
    **D. All four sections are involved**  
    *Correct: D. PRETEXT Stage IV: All four sections are involved.*

55. **Which of the following factors is NOT considered in the PRETEXT staging system?**  
    A. Local extension  
    B. Multifocality  
    C. Rupture  
    **D. Serum AFP level**  
    *Correct: D. PRETEXT staging considers localextension, multifocality, rupture, and metastasis, but not serum AFP level.*

56. **Which of the following is true about the treatment of hepatoblastoma?**  
    A. It is highly resistant to chemotherapy  
    **B. Multiple studies support the effectiveness of systemic chemotherapy combined with complete surgical resection**  
    C. Liver transplantation is the first-line treatment for all cases  
    D. Radiation therapy is the primary treatment modality  
    *Correct: B. Multiple studies support the effectiveness of systemic chemotherapy combined with complete surgical resection of the primary hepatic tumor.*

57. **What is the key factor determining survival in children with malignant liver tumors?**  
    A. Age at diagnosis  
    B. Serum AFP level  
    **C. Complete resection of the primary tumor**  
    D. Response to chemotherapy  
    *Correct: C. Survival depends on removal of the primary liver tumor, when imaging suggests that complete resection is feasible.*

58. **Which of the following is true about hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in children?**  
    A. It responds well to current chemotherapy agents  
    B. Long-term survival is possible without complete resection  
    **C. It remains extremely resistant to current chemotherapy agents**  
    D. It rarely involves vascular structures  
    *Correct: C. For more than a quarter century, no significant progress has been made in treatment of the pediatric population with HCC. This tumor remains extremely resistant to current chemotherapy agents.*

59. **Why is complete resection often impossible in children with hepatocellular carcinoma?**  
    A. Due to the small size of children's livers  
    **B. Because of a high incidence of multifocality, extrahepatic extension, vascular invasion, and distant metastases**  
    C. Due to the high risk of postoperative liver failure  
    D. Because these tumors are typically located in the porta hepatis  
    *Correct: B. Because of a high incidence of multifocality within the liver, extrahepatic extension to regional lymph nodes, vascular invasion, and distant metastases, complete resection is often impossible.*

60. **Which vascular structures are commonly involved by hepatocellular carcinoma in children?**  
    A. Portal vein only  
    B. Hepatic veins only  
    **C. Portal and hepatic venous branches, and sometimes the vena cava**  
    D. Hepatic artery only  
    *Correct: C. Infiltration with thrombosis of portal and hepatic venous branches is common, and even the vena cava may be involved.*

61. **Which of the following is a risk factor for the development of hepatocellular carcinoma in children?**  
    A. Hepatitis A infection  
    B. Obesity  
    **C. Cirrhosis**  
    D. Diabetes mellitus  
    *Correct: C. The cirrhosis found in a number of HCC livers may preclude an extensive resection.*

62. **Which of the following is true about the epidemiology of primary liver cancer in children?**  
    A. It is more common in adolescents than in infants  
    **B. The overall incidence is 16.5 cases per 1 million children in the 0- to 4-year age group**  
    C. It constitutes over 10% of all pediatric solid tumors  
    D. It is equally common in all age groups of children  
    *Correct: B. The overall incidence of primary liver cancer, as published by the SEER program, is 16.5 cases per 1 million children in the 0- to 4-year age group.*

63. **What percentage of all pediatric solid tumors do liver cancers constitute?**  
    A. Less than 0.1%  
    B. 0.1-0.5%  
    **C. 0.5% to 2%**  
    D. 5-10%  
    *Correct: C. Liver cancers constitute 0.5% to 2% of all pediatric solid tumors.*

64. **What percentage of abdominal tumors in childhood are liver cancers?**  
    A. 1%  
    B. 2.5%  
    **C. About 5%**  
    D. 10%  
    *Correct: C. Liver cancers constitute about 5% of abdominal tumors in childhood.*

65. **Which of the following is true about the age distribution of primary liver cancer in children?**  
    A. It is most common in adolescents  
    B. It has a bimodal distribution with peaks in infancy and adolescence  
    **C. The incidence is highest in the 0- to 4-year age group**  
    D. It is equally distributed across all childhood age groups  
    *Correct: C. The overall incidence of primary liver cancer is 16.5 cases per 1 million children in the 0- to 4-year age group, which is higher than in older age groups (0.5 per 1 million in 5-9 years, 0.9 in 10-14 years, and 1.5 in 14-19 years).*

66. **Which of the following is the most common site of metastasis for neuroblastoma in children?**  
    A. Brain  
    B. Lungs  
    **C. Liver**  
    D. Bones  
    *Correct: C. The text mentions that the liver is a relatively frequent site of metastatic disease in childhood for various malignancies including neuroblastoma.*

67. **Which of the following malignancies is NOT mentioned as commonly metastasizing to the liver in children?**  
    A. Neuroblastoma  
    B. Rhabdomyosarcoma  
    C. Wilms tumor  
    **D. Ewing sarcoma**  
    *Correct: D. The text mentions: "Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, rhabdoid tumors, Wilms tumor, desmoplastic small round-cell tumor, adrenal cortical carcinoma, osteogenic sarcomas, and a host of other malignancies may metastasize to the liver." Ewing sarcoma is not specifically mentioned.*

68. **Which of the following is true about the treatment of rhabdoid tumors of the liver?**  
    A. They respond well to standard chemotherapy  
    **B. They are poorly responsive to standard cytotoxic chemotherapy**  
    C. They are typically treated with radiation therapy alone  
    D. Liver transplantation is always curative  
    *Correct: B. Rhabdoid tumors of the liver are rare, aggressive, and poorly responsive to standard cytotoxic chemotherapy.*

69. **Which chromosome abnormality is associated with congenital disseminated malignant rhabdoid tumor?**  
    A. Chromosome 11q13  
    B. Chromosome 13q14  
    **C. Chromosome 22q11**  
    D. Chromosome 17p13  
    *Correct: C. Congenital disseminated malignant rhabdoid tumor demonstrates abnormalities of chromosome 22q11.*

70. **Which of the following is true about angiosarcoma of the liver in children?**  
    A. It is the most common primary liver tumor in children  
    B. It has an excellent response to chemotherapy  
    **C. It may develop from malignant transformation of infantile hemangioma or hemangioendothelioma**  
    D. It is typically diagnosed in infants younger than 6 months  
    *Correct: C. A multi-institutional case series found evidence of either malignant transformation from, or concomitant development with, infantile hemangioma or hemangioendothelioma in 7 of 8 patients.*

71. **Which of the following is true about the prognosis of embryonal sarcoma of the liver?**  
    A. It has an excellent prognosis with surgery alone  
    B. It responds well to chemotherapy  
    **C. These tumors are highly resistant to treatment**  
    D. Long-term survival exceeds 90%  
    *Correct: C. The text states: "These tumors are highly resistant to treatment."*

72. **What is the recommended treatment for embryonal sarcoma of the liver when disease is confined to the liver?**  
    A. Observation  
    B. Chemotherapy alone  
    **C. Resection if possible**  
    D. Radiation therapy  
    *Correct: C. "Disease confined to the liver should be resected if possible."*

73. **Which chemotherapy approach is warranted for embryonal sarcoma of the liver?**  
    A. Standard leukemia-type chemotherapy  
    **B. Dose-intense, antisarcoma-type chemotherapy**  
    C. Targeted molecular therapy  
    D. High-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue  
    *Correct: B. "Treatment with dose-intense, antisarcoma-type chemotherapy is also warranted."*

74. **What is the typical outcome for children with embryonal sarcoma of the liver?**  
    A. Complete cure is common with current therapies  
    **B. An initial period of control is feasible, but these tumors are likely to recur and metastasize**  
    C. They usually respond permanently to multimodal therapy  
    D. The prognosis is excellent regardless of treatment  
    *Correct: B. "Although an initial period of control is feasible, these tumors are likely to recur and metastasize."*

75. **Which of the following is true about malignant germ cell tumors of the liver?**  
    **A. They are very rare**  
    B. They are the most common primary liver tumors in children  
    C. They do not respond to chemotherapy  
    D. They are always benign  
    *Correct: A. "Primary malignant germ cell tumors of the liver are very rare..."*

76. **Which of the following tumor types may present as primary liver tumors in children?**  
    A. Glioblastoma  
    B. Medulloblastoma  
    **C. Teratoma**  
    D. Ependymoma  
    *Correct: C. "Primary malignant germ cell tumors of the liver are very rare and may present as teratomas, choriocarcinomas, or yolk sac tumors."*

77. **Which of the following is a treatment option for primary malignant germ cell tumors of the liver in children?**  
    A. Radiation therapy alone  
    **B. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by resection**  
    C. Liver transplantation as first-line treatment  
    D. Observation  
    *Correct: B. "In childhood, these may respond well to neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by resection."*

78. **Which of the following is true about the liver as a site of metastasis in children?**  
    A. It is uncommon for malignancies to metastasize to the liver  
    **B. It is a relatively frequent site of metastatic disease in childhood**  
    C. It is the most common site of metastasis for all childhood malignancies  
    D. Metastases to the liver always indicate terminal disease  
    *Correct: B. "The liver is a relatively frequent site of metastatic disease in childhood."*

79. **Which of the following malignancies is mentioned as metastasizing to the liver in children?**  
    A. Retinoblastoma  
    B. Medulloblastoma  
    **C. Osteogenic sarcoma**  
    D. All of the above  
    *Correct: C. "Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, rhabdoid tumors, Wilms tumor, desmoplastic small round-cell tumor, adrenal cortical carcinoma, osteogenic sarcomas, and a host of other malignancies may metastasize to the liver."*

80. **Which of the following is true about the surgical approach to metastatic liver lesions in children?**  
    A. All metastatic lesions should be resected  
    B. Resection always improves survival  
    **C. Few data are available to determine the correct surgical approach**  
    D. Liver transplantation is the standard of care  
    *Correct: C. "Few data are available to determine the correct surgical approach to these lesions."*

81. **Which of the following is true about the Liver Cancer Study Group of Japan's findings on hepatoblastoma?**  
    A. They found hepatoblastoma to be extremely rare  
    **B. They identified 30 hepatoblastomas (0.6%) in a cohort of 4658 patients of all ages**  
    C. They reported no cases of hepatoblastoma in children  
    D. They found hepatoblastoma to be the most common liver tumor in adults  
    *Correct: B. "The Liver Cancer Study Group of Japan identified 30 hepatoblastomas (0.6%) in a cohort of 4658 patients of all ages diagnosed during a 2-year period."*

82. **Which of the following is true about the epidemiology of hepatoblastoma?**  
    A. It is more common in adults than in children  
    **B. It comprises less than 1% of hepatic malignancies when adult age groups are included**  
    C. It accounts for over 50% of liver tumors in adolescents  
    D. It is equally common across all age groups  
    *Correct: B. "Hepatoblastoma... comprises less than 1% of hepatic malignancies when adult age groups are included."*

83. **Which tumor markers should be included in the diagnostic evaluation of suspected liver tumors in children?**  
    A. CA-125 and CEA  
    B. PSA and alkaline phosphatase  
    **C. Serum AFP and β-hCG**  
    D. LDH and ferritin  
    *Correct: C. "tumor markers that should include serum AFP and b-hCG."*

84. **Which of the following is true about the PRETEXT staging system update?**  
    A. It was developed for adult liver tumors  
    B. It focuses primarily on tumor histology  
    **C. It was recently updated and clarified to streamline its use in clinical trials**  
    D. It replaced the Milan criteria for liver transplantation  
    *Correct: C. "The PRETEXT system was recently updated and clarified to streamline its use in clinical trials."*

85. **Which of the following is true about the treatment of malignant liver tumors in children?**  
    A. Chemotherapy alone is sufficient for cure  
    **B. Complete surgical resection of the primary tumor is essential for survival**  
    C. Radiation therapy is the primary treatment modality  
    D. Liver transplantation is contraindicated  
    *Correct: B. "Survival depends on removal of the primary liver tumor, when imaging suggests that complete resection is feasible."*

86. **Which of the following is a characteristic feature of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (FLH)?**  
    A. It is most common in infants  
    B. It has a worse prognosis than standard HCC  
    **C. It tends to grow as a single mass**  
    D. It is associated with cirrhosis in most cases  
    *Correct: C. "The tendency of FLH to grow slowly, as a single mass, compared with the early multifocality of standard HCC."*

87. **Which of the following is true about the association between hepatic adenomas and high-estrogen environments?**  
    A. Hepatic adenomas only occur in high-estrogen environments  
    B. High-estrogen environments protect against hepatic adenomas  
    **C. Both FNH and adenomas have been correlated with a high-estrogen environment**  
    D. High-estrogen environments cause malignant transformation of hepatic adenomas  
    *Correct: C. "Both tumors have been correlated with a high-estrogen environment."*

88. **Which of the following patients might develop hepatic adenomas as a result of medication use?**  
    A. A child receiving insulin for diabetes  
    **B. A patient undergoing androgen therapy for hematologic disorders**  
    C. A child receiving antibiotics for recurrent infections  
    D. A patient receiving corticosteroids for asthma  
    *Correct: B. "Hepatic adenomas also have grown in patients undergoing androgen therapy for hematologic disorders, after danazol use, and in woman on oral contraceptives."*

89. **Which imaging technique may help discriminate between hepatic adenoma and focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH)?**  
    A. Standard ultrasound  
    B. Non-contrast CT  
    **C. Superparamagnetic oxide–enhanced MRI**  
    D. Plain X-ray  
    *Correct: C. "Superparamagnetic oxide–enhanced MRI may discriminate between hepatic adenoma and FNH."*

90. **Which of the following is a reason to resect hepatic adenomas in children?**  
    A. To prevent development of cirrhosis  
    B. To improve liver function tests  
    **C. Uncertainty about future malignant degeneration**  
    D. To reduce serum AFP levels  
    *Correct: C. "It is best to remove adenomas because of the difficulty of differentiating them from low-grade HCCs, uncertainty about future malignant degeneration, and the possibility of rupture and hemorrhage."*

91. **Which surgical procedure has been used successfully for hepatic adenomas in children?**  
    A. Right hepatectomy  
    **B. Extended left hepatectomy**  
    C. Total hepatectomy  
    D. Liver transplantation  
    *Correct: B. "An anatomic liver resection usually is required, and we have used extended left hepatectomy successfully in children to treat this lesion."*

92. **Which minimally invasive technique has been used for resection of benign liver tumors in children?**  
    A. Robotic surgery  
    **B. Laparoscopic resection**  
    C. Endoscopic resection  
    D. Percutaneous laser ablation  
    *Correct: B. "Laparoscopic resection of these lesions has also been done."*

93. **Which ablation technique has become an option for treatment of hepatic adenomas in children?**  
    A. Cryoablation  
    **B. Percutaneous radiofrequency ablation**  
    C. Microwave ablation  
    D. Ethanol ablation  
    *Correct: B. "Percutaneous RFA has recently become an option for treatment."*

94. **Which of the following is true about hemangioblastoma of the liver in children?**  
    A. It is the most common liver tumor in children  
    B. It typically presents with massive hemorrhage  
    **C. Distant metastases are uncommon**  
    D. It is always associated with neurofibromatosis  
    *Correct: C. "In infancy and childhood, these lesions appear very cellular, but distant metastases are uncommon."*

95. **Which syndrome is associated with hemangioblastoma of the liver?**  
    A. Neurofibromatosis type 1  
    B. Tuberous sclerosis  
    **C. von Hippel-Lindau disease**  
    D. Li-Fraumeni syndrome  
    *Correct: C. "Hemangioblastoma of the liver usually is associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease."*

96. **What is the treatment of choice for symptomatic hemangioblastoma of the liver?**  
    A. Chemotherapy  
    B. Radiation therapy  
    **C. Complete resection**  
    D. Observation  
    *Correct: C. "Complete resection should be performed and is usually curative."*

97. **Which of the following is true about the use of interferon-alpha 2a for hemangioblastomas?**  
    A. It is the first-line treatment  
    B. It has shown dramatic resolution of liver lesions  
    **C. It has been used for central nervous system and retinal lesions with limited success**  
    D. It is contraindicated in children  
    *Correct: C. "Hemangioblastomas of the central nervous system and retina have been treated with IFN-a2a but without striking resolution, although two retinal lesions showed shrinkage."*

98. **Which of the following is true about malignant peripheral nerve cell tumors metastasizing to the liver?**  
    A. They are the most common cause of liver metastases in children  
    **B. The text mentions them as one of "a host of other malignancies" that may metastasize to the liver**  
    C. They always present with elevated AFP  
    D. They respond exceptionally well to chemotherapy  
    *Correct: B. The text states: "Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, rhabdoid tumors, Wilms tumor, desmoplastic small round-cell tumor, adrenal cortical carcinoma, osteogenic sarcomas, and a host of other malignancies may metastasize to the liver."*

99. **Which of the following is true about colon cancer in children?**  
    A. It is the most common malignancy in children  
    B. It typically spreads through the portal system  
    **C. Approximately 50% of these patients have signet ring tumors**  
    D. It rarely involves the peritoneum  
    *Correct: C. "Colon cancer can occur in childhood. Approximately 50% of these patients have signet ring tumors."*

100. **How does colon cancer typically spread in children?**  
     A. Through the portal system to the liver  
     **B. Over peritoneal surfaces**  
     C. Through lymphatic channels to regional lymph nodes only  
     D. Hematogenously to the lungs  
     *Correct: B. "The pattern of spread is over peritoneal surfaces, rather than through the portal system, and hepatic metastases usually occur late despite massive peritoneal disease."*

101. **Which of the following is true about the liver's capacity for regeneration after resection in children?**  
     A. It is less than in adults  
     B. It takes years to regenerate  
     **C. Long-term hepatic regeneration and function is good after resection**  
     D. Regeneration does not occur in infants  
     *Correct: C. The text cites a reference about "Long-term hepatic regeneration and function in infants and children following liver resection."*

102. **Which of the following is true about the incidence of primary malignant liver tumors in Western nations?**  
     A. They constitute over 10% of childhood malignancies  
     **B. They constitute approximately 1.7% of childhood malignancies**  
     C. They are the most common childhood malignancy  
     D. They constitute about 10% of abdominal tumors in childhood  
     *Correct: B. "Primary malignant liver tumors constitute approximately 1.7% of childhood malignancies in Western nations."*

103. **Which of the following is true about the SEER program data on primary liver cancer incidence?**  
     A. The highest incidence is in the 14-19 year age group  
     B. The incidence is less than 0.1 cases per 1 million in the 0-4 year age group  
     **C. The incidence is 16.5 cases per 1 million in the 0-4 year age group**  
     D. The incidence steadily decreases with age  
     *Correct: C. "The overall incidence of primary liver cancer, as published by the SEER program, is 16.5 cases per 1 million children in the 0- to 4-year age group..."*

104. **Which of the following is true about the age distribution of hepatoblastoma?**  
     **A. It is most common in children younger than 5 years**  
     B. It is most common in adolescents  
     C. It has equal distribution across all age groups  
     D. It is most common in infants younger than 6 months  
     *Correct: A. "Hepatoblastoma accounts for 91% to 96% of primary hepatic tumors in children younger than 5 years."*

105. **Which of the following is true about the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma in infants?**  
     A. It is very common in infants  
     B. It accounts for over 50% of liver tumors in infants  
     **C. It is rare in infancy**  
     D. It is the most common liver tumor in infants  
     *Correct: C. "Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for 22% to 23% of pediatric liver tumors but is rare in infancy."*

106. **Which of the following is a potential pitfall in historic series of hepatocellular carcinoma in infants?**  
     A. Overdiagnosis due to improved imaging techniques  
     **B. Misdiagnosis of some early hepatoblastomas as HCC**  
     C. Underreporting due to lack of awareness  
     D. Confusion with benign liver tumors  
     *Correct: B. "Historic series without pathology review may report a higher rate of infantile HCC owing to misdiagnosis of some early hepatoblastomas."*

107. **Which of the following is true about the Liver Cancer Study Group of Japan's findings on hepatocellular carcinoma in young children?**  
     A. They found numerous cases in children age 4 years or younger  
     **B. They reported no cases in children age 4 years or younger**  
     C. They found hepatocellular carcinoma to be the most common liver tumor in this age group  
     D. They recommended universal screening for HCC in children under 5  
     *Correct: B. "The Lung Cancer Study Group of Japan reported no cases in children age 4 years or younger in a series of 2286 patients with histologically reviewed tumors."*

108. **Which of the following is true about the PRETEXT staging system criteria?**  
     A. It is based solely on tumor size  
     B. It incorporates serum tumor markers  
     **C. It classifies tumors based on local extension, multifocality, rupture, and metastasis**  
     D. It is identical to the staging system used for adults  
     *Correct: C. "Additional criteria added in 2005 further classify these tumors based on localextension, multifocality, rupture, and metastasis."*

109. **Which of the following is true about the PRETEXT Stage II classification?**  
     A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free  
     **B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free**  
     C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free  
     D. All four sections are involved  
     *Correct: B. PRETEXT Stage II: One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free.*

110. **Which of the following is true about the PRETEXT Stage III classification?**  
     A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free  
     B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free  
     **C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free**  
     D. All four sections are involved  
     *Correct: C. PRETEXT Stage III: Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free.*

111. **Which of the following is true about the PRETEXT staging system?**  
     A. It was developed for benign liver tumors  
     **B. It was developed by the SIOPEL group for primary malignant liver tumors of childhood**  
     C. It is used worldwide for adult liver cancer staging  
     D. It has not been updated since its initial publication  
     *Correct: B. "PRETEXT: A revised staging system for primary malignant liver tumours of childhood developed by the SIOPEL group."*

112. **Which of the following is true about the role of liver transplantation in hepatocellular carcinoma?**  
     A. It is contraindicated in children with HCC  
     **B. It has been used more widely due to the lack of success with standard therapies**  
     C. It is the first-line treatment for all cases of HCC  
     D. It has worse outcomes than resection in all cases  
     *Correct: B. "Because standard therapies have proven unsuccessful, liver transplantation has been used more widely."*

113. **Which criteria have been extrapolated from adult liver transplantation to pediatric hepatocellular carcinoma?**  
     A. Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) criteria  
     **B. Milan criteria**  
     C. Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score  
     D. Child-Pugh classification  
     *Correct: B. "The Milan criteria used for adults have been extrapolated to children."*

114. **According to the Milan criteria for children with hepatocellular carcinoma, what is the maximum size for a single tumor to be eligible for liver transplantation?**  
     A. 2 cm  
     B. 3 cm  
     **C. 5 cm**  
     D. 10 cm  
     *Correct: C. "They stipulate a single tumor no larger than 5 cm in diameter..."*

115. **According to the Milan criteria for children with hepatocellular carcinoma, what is the maximum size for multiple tumors to be eligible for liver transplantation?**  
     A. Any size as long as there are fewer than 3 tumors  
     B. Each tumor must be 1 cm or less in diameter  
     **C. As many as three tumors each 3 cm or less in diameter**  
     D. A total tumor burden of less than 5 cm  
     *Correct: C. "As many as three tumors each 3 cm or less in diameter."*

116. **Which of the following is an exclusion criterion for liver transplantation in children with hepatocellular carcinoma according to the Milan criteria?**  
     A. Age younger than 2 years  
     B. Elevated AFP levels  
     **C. Macroscopic portal vein invasion**  
     D. Bilobar disease  
     *Correct: C. "An absence of macroscopic portal vein invasions, and absence of extrahepatic disease."*

117. **Which of the following is true about the evidence supporting the use of Milan criteria in children with hepatocellular carcinoma?**  
     A. There is strong evidence from multiple randomized trials  
     B. It has been validated in large pediatric studies  
     **C. No current data support the efficacy of using the Milan criteria in this population**  
     D. It is the standard of care based on decades of experience  
     *Correct: C. "However, no current data support the efficacy of using the Milan criteria in this population."*

118. **Which database included information on patients with hepatocellular carcinoma who received orthotopic liver transplantation?**  
     A. SEER database  
     **B. UNOS database**  
     C. Medicare database  
     D. National Cancer Database  
     *Correct: B. "The UNOS database included information on 41 patients with HCC who received OLT from 1987..."*

119. **Which of the following is true about mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver?**  
     A. It is the most common malignant liver tumor in infants  
     **B. It is a benign tumor that can present in infancy or teenage years**  
     C. It always requires aggressive chemotherapy  
     D. It is typically diagnosed in adulthood  
     *Correct: B. "Two-thirds of these tumors are diagnosed in infants younger than 1 year, although presentation in the teenage years has been described."*

120. **Which of the following is true about the incidence of mesenchymal hamartoma among space-occupying liver lesions?**  
     A. It accounts for over 50% of cases  
     B. It is extremely rare, with fewer than 10 cases ever reported  
     **C. In one study, 4 of 134 patients with space-occupying liver lesions had mesenchymal hamartomas**  
     D. It is the most common liver tumor in adults  
     *Correct: C. "In one study, 4 of 134 patients with space-occupying liver lesions had mesenchymal hamartomas."*

121. **Which of the following is true about mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver?**  
     A. It is always malignant  
     B. It typically presents with markedly elevated AFP  
     **C. It is a benign tumor**  
     D. It requires immediate chemotherapy  
     *Correct: C. Mesenchymal hamartoma is listed among benign hepatic tumors in the text.*

122. **Which of the following is true about the gender distribution of hepatic hemangiomata in children?**  
     A. Equal incidence in both genders  
     **B. More common in girls by 2:1**  
     C. More common in boys by 2:1  
     D. Predominantly affects males  
     *Correct: B. "Hepatic hemangiomata are more common in girls by 2:1."*

123. **Which of the following vascular abnormalities may be associated with congestive heart failure in children with liver tumors?**  
     A. Capillary hemangiomas  
     **B. Venous malformations, cavernous hemangiomata, and arteriovenous malformations**  
     C. Lymphatic malformations  
     D. Simple hemangiomas  
     *Correct: B. "Venous malformations, cavernous hemangiomata, and arteriovenous malformations may be associated with significant shunting that results in congestive heart failure."*

124. **Which of the following is true about the overall incidence of endothelial-lined vascular tumors of the liver in childhood?**  
     A. It is precisely known and well-documented  
     **B. It is probably unknown because many are asymptomatic**  
     C. It is estimated to be over 10% of all childhood cancers  
     D. It has been declining due to vaccination programs  
     *Correct: B. "The overall incidence of endothelial-lined vascular tumors of the liver in childhood is probably unknown because many are asymptomatic."*

125. **Which of the following is true about the presentation of vascular tumors of the liver in children?**  
     A. They always present with abdominal pain  
     B. They typically present with jaundice  
     **C. Many are asymptomatic**  
     D. They always present with tumor rupture  
     *Correct: C. "The overall incidence of endothelial-lined vascular tumors of the liver in childhood is probably unknown because many are asymptomatic."*

126. **Which of the following is true about patients who present with hemorrhagic shock due to rupture of a vascular tumor?**  
     A. They can be managed conservatively with observation  
     **B. They usually require hepatic resection**  
     C. They should undergo immediate liver transplantation  
     D. Embolization is always contraindicated  
     *Correct: B. "Patients who are seen in hemorrhagic shock with rupture of a vascular tumor usually require hepatic resection."*

127. **Which of the following is true about the frequency of asymptomatic vascular tumors discovered incidentally with modern imaging techniques?**  
     A. It is lower than in the past  
     **B. It is undoubtedly much higher than reflected in surgical or pathologic series**  
     C. It has remained constant over time  
     D. It is negligible  
     *Correct: B. "With modern imaging techniques, the frequency of asymptomatic vascular tumors discovered incidentally is undoubtedly much higher."*

128. **Which of the following is true about the relationship between focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) and previous cancer treatment?**  
     A. FNH is a common complication of radiation therapy  
     **B. FNH has been described in children previously treated for solid tumors**  
     C. FNH only occurs in children who have not received cancer treatment  
     D. Cancer treatment prevents the development of FNH  
     *Correct: B. "Focal nodular hyperplasia of the liver: a sequela of tumor therapy."*

129. **What is postulated to be the causal factor for focal nodular hyperplasia developing in children treated for other solid malignancies?**  
     A. Immunosuppression  
     **B. Vascular injury secondary to chemotherapy or radiation**  
     C. Genetic predisposition  
     D. Viral infection  
     *Correct: B. "These authors postulated that a vascular injury secondary to chemotherapy or radiation was the causal factor."*

130. **Which of the following is true about the malignant potential of hepatic adenomas?**  
     A. They never undergo malignant transformation  
     **B. Some unresected hepatic adenomas may develop hepatocellular carcinoma**  
     C. Malignant transformation occurs in over 50% of cases  
     D. They always transform into cholangiocarcinoma  
     *Correct: B. "In one report, 5 of 39 unresected hepatic adenomas developed HCC."*

131. **What percentage of unresected hepatic adenomas developed hepatocellular carcinoma in one report?**  
     A. 1.3%  
     B. 5.1%  
     **C. 12.8% (5 of 39)**  
     D. 25.6%  
     *Correct: C. "In one report, 5 of 39 unresected hepatic adenomas developed HCC."*

132. **Which of the following is true about the size of hepatic adenomas in childhood?**  
     A. They are typically small, less than 2 cm  
     **B. They may attain great size, with an average tumor size of 7.5 cm in one report**  
     C. They never exceed 5 cm in diameter  
     D. Size does not affect symptoms  
     *Correct: B. "In one report of six cases in childhood, the average tumor size was 7.5 cm (range, 2.5-10 cm)."*

133. **Which lobe of the liver is most commonly affected by hepatic adenomas in children?**  
     A. Left lobe  
     **B. Right lobe**  
     C. Caudate lobe  
     D. Quadrate lobe  
     *Correct: B. "The tumor was localized to the right lobe in four of the six and was bilobar in the remaining two."*

134. **Which imaging technique may help discriminate between hepatic adenoma and focal nodular hyperplasia?**  
     A. Standard CT scan  
     B. Ultrasound with Doppler  
     **C. Superparamagnetic oxide–enhanced MRI**  
     D. PET scan  
     *Correct: C. "Superparamagnetic oxide–enhanced MRI may discriminate between hepatic adenoma and FNH."*

135. **Which of the following is a reason to remove hepatic adenomas in children?**  
     A. To prevent development of cirrhosis  
     B. To improve overall survival in all cases  
     **C. Possibility of rupture and hemorrhage**  
     D. To reduce the risk of portal hypertension  
     *Correct: C. "It is best to remove adenomas because of the difficulty of differentiating them from low-grade HCCs, uncertainty about future malignant degeneration, and the possibility of rupture and hemorrhage."*

136. **Which surgical procedure has been used for hepatic adenomas involving the left side of the liver?**  
     A. Right hepatectomy  
     **B. Extended left hepatectomy**  
     C. Caudate lobectomy  
     D. Segmental resection only  
     *Correct: B. "An anatomic liver resection usually is required, and we have used extended left hepatectomy successfully in children to treat this lesion."*

137. **Which minimally invasive technique has been used for benign hepatic adenomas?**  
     A. Endoscopic mucosal resection  
     **B. Percutaneous radiofrequency ablation**  
     C. Transarterial chemoembolization  
     D. Photodynamic therapy  
     *Correct: B. "Contemporary management of benign hepatic adenoma using percutaneous radiofrequency ablation."*

138. **Which of the following is true about the use of embolization for hepatic tumors?**  
     A. It is only used for malignant tumors  
     B. It is the first-line treatment for all liver tumors  
     **C. It is an option for unresectable lesions**  
     D. It is contraindicated in children  
     *Correct: C. "Embolization of unresectable lesions is another [option]."*

139. **Which of the following is true about embryonal sarcoma (undifferentiated sarcoma) of the liver?**  
     A. It is the most common liver tumor in infants  
     **B. It is a rare primary hepatic neoplasm that occurs in older children**  
     C. It typically occurs in children younger than 2 years  
     D. It has an excellent prognosis with surgery alone  
     *Correct: B. "Embryonal sarcoma, also known as malignant mesenchymoma or undifferentiated sarcoma in the older literature, is a rare primary hepatic neoplasm that occurs in older children."*

140. **What percentage of primary liver tumors does embryonal sarcoma represent?**  
     A. Over 10%  
     B. 5-10%  
     **C. 0.2% (2 cases out of 1102)**  
     D. Less than 0.1%  
     *Correct: C. "In one study, 2 cases were reported out of 1102 (0.2%) primary liver tumors analyzed."*

141. **How many cases of embryonal sarcoma have been reported in the literature?**  
     A. Fewer than 50  
     B. 50-100  
     **C. Fewer than 200**  
     D. Over 500  
     *Correct: C. "Fewer than 200 cases have been reported in the literature."*

142. **Which age group is most commonly affected by embryonal sarcoma?**  
     A. Infants  
     B. Toddlers (1-3 years)  
     **C. Older children (5-16 years)**  
     D. Adolescents only  
     *Correct: C. "The age at diagnosis ranges from 5 to 16 years."*

143. **What percentage of malignant liver tumors in children 6 to 10 years of age is constituted by embryonal sarcoma?**  
     A. 5%  
     B. 10%  
     **C. 14%**  
     D. 25%  
     *Correct: C. "Embryonal sarcoma constitutes 14% of malignant liver tumors occurring in children 6 to 10 years of age."*

144. **Which of the following is true about embryonal sarcoma of the liver?**  
     A. It is more common in infants  
     **B. Many recently reported patients were older than 10 years**  
     C. It accounts for the majority of liver tumors in children under 5  
     D. It has a better prognosis than hepatoblastoma  
     *Correct: B. "Embryonal sarcoma constitutes 14% of malignant liver tumors occurring in children 6 to 10 years of age; however, many of the patients reported recently were older than 10 years."*

145. **Which of the following is true about the treatment of embryonal sarcoma?**  
     A. It is highly responsive to standard chemotherapy  
     B. Radiation therapy is the primary treatment  
     **C. Resection is indicated if disease is confined to the liver**  
     D. Liver transplantation is always required  
     *Correct: C. "Disease confined to the liver should be resected if possible."*

146. **Which type of chemotherapy is warranted for embryonal sarcoma of the liver?**  
     A. Leukemia-type chemotherapy  
     **B. Antisarcoma-type chemotherapy**  
     C. Lymphoma-type chemotherapy  
     D. Neuroblastoma-type chemotherapy  
     *Correct: B. "Treatment with dose-intense, antisarcoma-type chemotherapy is also warranted."*

147. **What is the typical outcome for children with embryonal sarcoma of the liver?**  
     A. Complete cure is common  
     **B. An initial period of control is feasible, but recurrence and metastasis are likely**  
     C. It always responds permanently to treatment  
     D. The prognosis is excellent regardless of treatment  
     *Correct: B. "Although an initial period of control is feasible, these tumors are likely to recur and metastasize."*

148. **Which of the following is true about rhabdoid tumors of the liver?**  
     A. They are the most common liver tumors in children  
     B. They have an excellent prognosis with standard treatment  
     **C. They are rare, aggressive, and poorly responsive to standard chemotherapy**  
     D. They are always primary to the liver  
     *Correct: C. "Rhabdoid tumors of the liver: rare, aggressive, and poorly responsive to standard cytotoxic chemotherapy."*

149. **Which chromosome abnormality is associated with congenital disseminated malignant rhabdoid tumor?**  
     A. Chromosome 11p15  
     B. Chromosome 13q14  
     **C. Chromosome 22q11**  
     D. Chromosome 17p13  
     *Correct: C. "Congenital disseminated malignant rhabdoid tumor: a distinct clinicopathologic entity demonstrating abnormalities of chromosome 22q11."*

150. **Which of the following is true about the origin of rhabdoid tumors?**  
     A. They always originate in the liver  
     **B. They most commonly originate from the kidney and can metastasize to liver**  
     C. They only occur as primary liver tumors  
     D. They originate from hematopoietic cells  
     *Correct: B. "Rhabdoid tumor most commonly originates from the kidney and can metastasize to liver."*

151. **Which of the following is true about the pattern of hepatic metastases in rhabdoid tumor?**  
     A. It typically presents as a single metastasis  
     **B. The pattern is usually diffuse and not amenable to surgical resection**  
     C. Metastases are always resectable  
     D. It rarely involves the liver  
     *Correct: B. "The pattern for hepatic metastases is usually diffuse and is not amenable to surgical resection."*

152. **Which chemotherapy protocols are typically used for rhabdoid tumors of the liver?**  
     A. Leukemia protocols  
     **B. Protocols suitable for sarcoma**  
     C. Lymphoma protocols  
     D. Neuroblastoma protocols  
     *Correct: B. "Chemotherapy protocols suitable for sarcoma are usually used."*

153. **Which of the following is true about biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
     A. It is the most common type of rhabdomyosarcoma  
     **B. It is very rare**  
     C. It typically occurs in adults  
     D. It has an excellent prognosis regardless of treatment  
     *Correct: B. "Rhabdomyosarcoma of the liver and the ampulla of Vater, but not involving the bile ducts, also has been reported but is very rare."*

154. **What is the typical age range for diagnosis of biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
     A. Infancy  
     **B. 1 to 9 years, with an average age of 3 years**  
     C. 10 to 15 years  
     D. Adolescence  
     *Correct: B. "These tumors are usually diagnosed from 1 to 9 years of age, with an average age of 3 years."*

155. **Which gender is more frequently affected by biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
     **A. Males**  
     B. Females  
     C. Equal incidence in both genders  
     D. Gender predilection is unknown  
     *Correct: A. "These tumors... are seen more frequently in males."*

156. **Which symptom is commonly associated with biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
     A. Hematemesis  
     B. Melena  
     **C. Intermittent jaundice**  
     D. Hematuria  
     *Correct: C. "The typical presentation includes intermittent jaundice."*

157. **What is the long-term survival rate for biliary rhabdomyosarcoma?**  
     A. 10-20%  
     B. 30-40%  
     **C. 60-70%**  
     D. 80-90%  
     *Correct: C. "Long-term survival is considered to be 60% to 70% and is not dependent on resectability."*

158. **Which of the following is true about the cause of death in patients with unresectable malignant tumors of the extrahepatic biliary tract?**  
     A. Metastatic disease to the brain  
     B. Renal failure  
     **C. Local tumor effects including biliary sepsis**  
     D. Cardiac complications  
     *Correct: C. "Malignant tumors of the extrahepatic biliary tract often cause death due to the effects of local invasion, including biliary sepsis."*

159. **Which of the following is true about angiosarcoma of the liver in children?**  
     A. It is the most common primary liver tumor in children  
     B. It has an excellent response to chemotherapy  
     **C. In a multi-institutional case series, 7 of 8 patients showed evidence of malignant transformation from, or concomitant development with, infantile hemangioma or hemangioendothelioma**  
     D. It is typically diagnosed in infants younger than 6 months  
     *Correct: C. "A more recent, multi-institutional case series of 8 pediatric patients with hepatic angiosarcoma found evidence of either malignant transformation from, or concomitant development with, infantile hemangioma or hemangioendothelioma in 7 of 8 patients."*

160. **What was the outcome for pediatric patients with hepatic angiosarcoma who underwent orthotopic liver transplantation as part of multimodal therapy?**  
     A. All patients died within 1 year  
     B. Transplantation worsened the prognosis  
     **C. The transplanted patients were the only ones alive at publication, disease-free at 3.5 and 5.5 years**  
     D. Transplantation had no impact on survival  
     *Correct: C. "Two out of eight patients underwent orthotopic liver transplantation as a part of multimodal therapy, and these were the only two patients alive at the time of publication, disease-free at 3.5 years and 5.5 years, respectively."*

161. **Which of the following is true about primary malignant germ cell tumors of the liver?**  
     A. They are the most common primary liver tumors in children  
     B. They do not respond to chemotherapy  
     **C. They are very rare**  
     D. They are always malignant  
     *Correct: C. "Primary malignant germ cell tumors of the liver are very rare..."*

162. **Which types of germ cell tumors may present as primary tumors of the liver?**  
     A. Seminomas only  
     **B. Teratomas, choriocarcinomas, or yolk sac tumors**  
     C. Dysgerminomas only  
     D. Carcinoid tumors  
     *Correct: B. "Primary malignant germ cell tumors of the liver are very rare and may present as teratomas, choriocarcinomas, or yolk sac tumors."*

163. **Which chemotherapy regimen is typically used for malignant germ cell tumors of the liver in children?**  
     A. ABVD  
     **B. Cisplatin, ifosfamide, and bleomycin**  
     C. CHOP  
     D. VAC (vincristine, actinomycin D, cyclophosphamide)  
     *Correct: B. "Usually, a regimen containing cisplatin, ifosfamide, and bleomycin is used."*

164. **Which of the following is true about the response of malignant germ cell tumors of the liver to treatment in children?**  
     A. They are highly resistant to all treatments  
     **B. They may respond well to neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by resection**  
     C. They always require liver transplantation  
     D. They respond best to radiation therapy  
     *Correct: B. "In childhood, these may respond well to neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by resection."*

165. **Which of the following is true about the liver as a site for metastatic disease in children?**  
     A. It is uncommon for malignancies to metastasize to the liver  
     **B. It is a relatively frequent site of metastatic disease in childhood**  
     C. It is the most common site of metastasis for all childhood malignancies  
     D. Metastases to the liver always indicate terminal disease  
     *Correct: B. "The liver is a relatively frequent site of metastatic disease in childhood."*

166. **Which of the following malignancies is mentioned as commonly metastasizing to the liver in children?**  
     A. Retinoblastoma  
     B. Medulloblastoma  
     **C. Osteogenic sarcoma**  
     D. All of the above  
     *Correct: C. "Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, rhabdoid tumors, Wilms tumor, desmoplastic small round-cell tumor, adrenal cortical carcinoma, osteogenic sarcomas, and a host of other malignancies may metastasize to the liver."*

167. **Which of the following is true about the surgical approach to metastatic liver lesions in children?**  
     A. All metastatic lesions should be resected  
     B. Resection always improves survival  
     **C. Few data are available to determine the correct surgical approach**  
     D. Liver transplantation is the standard of care  
     *Correct: C. "Few data are available to determine the correct surgical approach to these lesions."*

168. **Which of the following is true about the use of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in children with metastatic liver disease?**  
     A. It is only used for primary liver tumors  
     **B. It may benefit patients with neuroendocrine tumors, gastrointestinal stromal tumors, and uveal melanoma**  
     C. It is contraindicated in all pediatric patients  
     D. It has been proven to cure metastatic disease  
     *Correct: B. "Beyond primary hepatic malignancy, patients with metastatic liver disease may also benefit from TACE, including patients with neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs), uveal melanoma, and other common pathology..."*

169. **For which of the following conditions is TACE most commonly indicated in patients with metastatic liver disease?**  
     A. Asymptomatic patients with slow-growing tumors  
     **B. Rapid progression of liver tumor with stable or absent extrahepatic disease and symptoms related to tumor bulk or hormonal excess**  
     C. Patients with extensive extrahepatic disease  
     D. Patients with normal liver function tests  
     *Correct: B. "The most common indications are rapid progression of liver tumor with stable or absent extrahepatic disease and symptoms related to tumor bulk or hormonal excess, especially among patients with NET."*

170. **Which of the following is true about the epidemiology of primary liver cancer in children according to the SEER program?**  
     A. The incidence is highest in the 14-19 year age group  
     B. The incidence is less than 0.1 cases per 1 million in the 0-4 year age group  
     **C. The incidence is 0.5 cases per 1 million in the 5-9 year age group**  
     D. The incidence steadily increases with age  
     *Correct: C. "The overall incidence of primary liver cancer, as published by the SEER program, is 16.5 cases per 1 million children in the 0- to 4-year age group, 0.5 cases per 1 million in the 5- to 9-year age group, 0.9 cases per 1 million in the 10- to 14-year age group, and 1.5 cases per 1 million in the 14- to 19-year age group."*

171. **Which of the following is true about the incidence of primary liver cancer in the 10-14 year age group according to the SEER program?**  
     A. 0.1 cases per 1 million  
     B. 0.5 cases per 1 million  
     **C. 0.9 cases per 1 million**  
     D. 1.5 cases per 1 million  
     *Correct: C. "The overall incidence of primary liver cancer, as published by the SEER program, is [...] 0.9 cases per 1 million in the 10- to 14-year age group..."*

172. **Which of the following is true about the incidence of primary liver cancer in the 14-19 year age group according to the SEER program?**  
     A. 0.1 cases per 1 million  
     B. 0.5 cases per 1 million  
     C. 0.9 cases per 1 million  
     **D. 1.5 cases per 1 million**  
     *Correct: D. "The overall incidence of primary liver cancer, as published by the SEER program, is [...] 1.5 cases per 1 million in the 14- to 19-year age group."*

173. **Which of the following is true about the relative frequency of liver cancers among abdominal tumors in childhood?**  
     A. They constitute less than 1% of abdominal tumors  
     B. They constitute 1-2% of abdominal tumors  
     **C. They constitute about 5% of abdominal tumors**  
     D. They constitute over 10% of abdominal tumors  
     *Correct: C. "Liver cancers constitute about 5% of abdominal tumors in childhood."*

174. **Which of the following is true about the relative frequency of liver cancers among all pediatric solid tumors?**  
     A. They constitute less than 0.1% of solid tumors  
     B. They constitute 0.1-0.4% of solid tumors  
     **C. They constitute 0.5% to 2% of solid tumors**  
     D. They constitute over 5% of solid tumors  
     *Correct: C. "Liver cancers constitute 0.5% to 2% of all pediatric solid tumors."*

175. **Which of the following is true about the Liver Cancer Study Group of Japan's findings on hepatoblastoma?**  
     A. They found hepatoblastoma to be extremely rare  
     **B. They identified 30 hepatoblastomas (0.6%) in a cohort of 4658 patients of all ages**  
     C. They reported no cases of hepatoblastoma in children  
     D. They found hepatoblastoma to be the most common liver tumor in adults  
     *Correct: B. "The Liver Cancer Study Group of Japan identified 30 hepatoblastomas (0.6%) in a cohort of 4658 patients of all ages diagnosed during a 2-year period."*

176. **Which of the following is true about the epidemiology of hepatoblastoma?**  
     A. It is more common in adults than in children  
     **B. It comprises less than 1% of hepatic malignancies when adult age groups are included**  
     C. It accounts for over 50% of liver tumors in adolescents  
     D. It is equally common across all age groups  
     *Correct: B. "Hepatoblastoma... comprises less than 1% of hepatic malignancies when adult age groups are included."*

177. **Which of the following is true about the role of alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) in the diagnostic evaluation of liver tumors in children?**  
     A. It is only measured for research purposes  
     B. It is never elevated in malignant liver tumors  
     **C. It should be included in tumor markers for evaluation**  
     D. It is only useful for diagnosing hepatocellular carcinoma  
     *Correct: C. "tumor markers that should include serum AFP and b-hCG."*

178. **Which of the following is true about the role of beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) in the diagnostic evaluation of liver tumors in children?**  
     A. It is only measured for research purposes  
     B. It is never elevated in malignant liver tumors  
     **C. It should be included in tumor markers for evaluation**  
     D. It is only useful for diagnosing germ cell tumors outside the liver  
     *Correct: C. "tumor markers that should include serum AFP and b-hCG."*

179. **Which imaging modality is recommended to determine whether a liver mass is cystic or solid?**  
     A. Standard X-ray  
     B. CT scan without contrast  
     **C. Doppler US**  
     D. Bone scan  
     *Correct: C. "Doppler US is done to determine whether a mass is cystic or solid, determine the patency of the portal and hepatic veins and vena cava, and identify satellite lesions."*

180. **Which imaging modality provides information about the liver lesion and surrounding veins and bile ducts equivalent to MRI?**  
     A. Standard ultrasound  
     **B. CT portography**  
     C. PET scan  
     D. Plain X-ray  
     *Correct: B. "CT portography has been shown to give anatomic information equal to MRI."*

181. **Which of the following is true about the use of thoracic CT in the evaluation of suspected malignant liver tumors in children?**  
     A. It is primarily used to evaluate liver anatomy  
     B. It is used to assess for portal vein thrombosis  
     **C. It is done to evaluate for pulmonary metastases**  
     D. It is used to measure tumor markers  
     *Correct: C. While the text cuts off, "If a malignant tumor is suspected, thoracic CT is done to..." strongly implies it's for staging, which would include evaluation for pulmonary metastases.*

182. **Which of the following is true about the PRETEXT staging system?**  
     A. It is used for both benign and malignant liver tumors  
     **B. It is a staging system specifically for primary malignant liver tumors of childhood**  
     C. It was developed for adult hepatocellular carcinoma  
     D. It is based solely on tumor size  
     *Correct: B. PRETEXT is described as "a revised staging system for primary malignant liver tumours of childhood developed by the SIOPEL group."*

183. **How many stages are there in the PRETEXT staging system?**  
     A. 2  
     B. 3  
     **C. 4**  
     D. 5  
     *Correct: C. The PRETEXT staging has four stages (I-IV) as described in the text.*

184. **In PRETEXT staging, what does Stage I indicate?**  
     **A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free**  
     B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free  
     C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free  
     D. All four sections are involved  
     *Correct: A. PRETEXT Stage I: One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free.*

185. **In PRETEXT staging, what does Stage II indicate?**  
     A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free  
     **B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free**  
     C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free  
     D. All four sections are involved  
     *Correct: B. PRETEXT Stage II: One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free.*

186. **In PRETEXT staging, what does Stage III indicate?**  
     A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free  
     B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free  
     **C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free**  
     D. All four sections are involved  
     *Correct: C. PRETEXT Stage III: Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free.*

187. **In PRETEXT staging, what does Stage IV indicate?**  
     A. One section is involved, and three adjoining sections are free  
     B. One or two sections are involved, but two adjoining sections are free  
     C. Two or three sections are involved, and no two adjoining sections are free  
     **D. All four sections are involved**  
     *Correct: D. PRETEXT Stage IV: All four sections are involved.*

188. **Which of the following factors is considered in the PRETEXT staging system?**  
     A. Serum AFP level  
     B. Patient age  
     **C. Local extension**  
     D. Response to chemotherapy  
     *Correct: C. PRETEXT staging considers localextension, multifocality, rupture, and metastasis.*

189. **Which of the following factors is considered in the PRETEXT staging system?**  
     A. Serum bilirubin level  
     B. Liver function tests  
     **C. Multifocality**  
     D. Performance status
